rationale: Neuroimaging findings across all reported cohorts and cases of PLAA-related neurodevelopmental disorder with progressive microcephaly, spasticity, and brain anomalies (NDMSBA; OMIM #617527) consistently document corpus callosum hypoplasia/thinning, delayed or defective myelination/leukoencephalopathy, and progressive cerebral and/or cerebellar atrophy on serial brain MRI. While individual patients may exhibit additional structural variations (such as vermis atrophy, simplified gyral pattern, or cortical malformations like polymicrogyria/lissencephaly), no source contradicts the characterization of thin corpus callosum, delayed myelination, and progressive cerebral/cerebellar atrophy as hallmark neuroimaging features of this condition.

evidence.text: Neuroimaging in affected individuals during the first year of life demonstrated a thin corpus callosum, delayed myelination, and cerebral changes alongside progressive microcephaly resulting from biallelic PLAA mutations.
